pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction is directly opposite to north? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. East
   D. North-east

2. How many counties does Kenya have? (1 mark)
   A. 27
   B. 37
   C. 57
   D. 47

3. Which imaginary line crosses Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The railway line
   B. The boundary
   C. The river line
   D. The equator

4. Which ocean is found on the south-eastern side of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Indian Ocean
   B. Atlantic Ocean
   C. Arctic Ocean
   D. Pacific Ocean

5. What do we call a place where a river falls over a cliff? (1 mark)
   A. Waterfall
   B. Plateau
   C. Valley
   D. Plain

6. In many parts of Kenya, when do the long rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. June to August
   B. March to May
   C. January to February
   D. September only

7. Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm? (1 mark)
   A. In an open field
   B. Beside a river
   C. In a strong building
   D. Under a tall tree

8. If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on? (1 mark)
   A. On the side where there is no light
   B. The side with traffic behind
   C. In the middle of the road
   D. The side facing the oncoming traffic

9. In many parts of Kenya, when do the short rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. January only
   B. June to July
   C. October to December
   D. March to May

10. Fort Jesus is found in which town? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Eldoret
   C. Mombasa
   D. Nakuru

11. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. All useful jobs are important
   B. Small jobs do not matter
   C. Only doctors are important
   D. Only farming is important

12. How is money useful in trade? (1 mark)
   A. It stops trade
   B. It builds houses
   C. It grows crops
   D. It makes buying and selling easier

13. On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 70
   B. 70,000
   C. 700
   D. 7,000

14. What is culture? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of weather
   B. A kind of animal
   C. The way of life of a community
   D. A type of road

15. Why is traditional culture important? (1 mark)
   A. It makes people fight
   B. It gives identity and teaches values
   C. It stops all change
   D. It has no use

16. What is discipline? (1 mark)
   A. Controlling yourself and following rules
   B. Shouting
   C. Doing what you like
   D. Running away

17. Which is NOT allowed in Kenyan schools? (1 mark)
   A. Praising pupils
   B. Talking to pupils
   C. Guiding and counselling pupils
   D. Beating pupils

18. Why do schools have rules? (1 mark)
   A. To stop friendship
   B. To make pupils sad
   C. To keep everyone safe and help learning
   D. To stop lessons

19. Which of these is a human resource? (1 mark)
   A. A skilled farmer
   B. A lake
   C. A forest
   D. A mineral

20. Which item of clothing protects a worker's head in a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Scarf
   B. Helmet
   C. Skirt
   D. Sandals

21. Which is a service industry? (1 mark)
   A. A cement plant
   B. A dairy plant
   C. A hotel
   D. A sugar mill

22. What should you do when visiting a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Touch all machines
   C. Run around
   D. Stay with the group and not touch machines

23. What is an industry? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   C. A type of weather
   D. A kind of farm animal

24. What is a factory? (1 mark)
   A. A large building where goods are made with machines
   B. A school
   C. A hospital
   D. A market

25. What is an enterprise? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A business activity to make goods or provide services
   C. A weather chart
   D. A school rule

26. A group spent Ksh 400 and earned Ksh 700. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 300
   B. Ksh 1,100
   C. Ksh 400
   D. Ksh 700

27. What should you do if something online makes you feel scared? (1 mark)
   A. Reply angrily
   B. Meet the stranger
   C. Tell a trusted adult
   D. Keep it secret

28. What is a duty? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. Something you are expected to do
   C. A game
   D. Something you may not do

29. What is a peace garden? (1 mark)
   A. A place for fighting
   B. A garden where pupils can sit and be calm
   C. A car park
   D. A market

30. Which is a peace message? (1 mark)
   A. Get back at them
   B. Shout louder
   C. Talk, do not fight
   D. Fight for it

31. Why is it important to plan a peace-building activity? (1 mark)
   A. So that it wastes time
   B. So that nobody joins
   C. So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   D. So that it is cancelled

32. Which is a way to promote child rights in school? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Ignoring children with problems
   C. Making posters and songs on child protection
   D. Hiding problems

33. What does equality mean in an election? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers vote
   B. Some people have many votes
   C. Each person has one vote of equal value
   D. Only boys vote

34. A candidate gives sweets for votes. What is this? (1 mark)
   A. Kindness
   B. Fair campaigning
   C. Democracy
   D. Cheating

35. Which of these is a democratic process in school? (1 mark)
   A. A bully choosing leaders
   B. Punishing pupils who speak
   C. Ignoring pupils' ideas
   D. Electing a class monitor by voting

36. Which is a function of the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Beating pupils
   B. Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   C. Setting exams
   D. Collecting fees

37. Which of these is a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. A farmer
   B. A pastor
   C. A trader
   D. A driver

38. Who leads a location and is appointed by the national government? (1 mark)
   A. Village poet
   B. Chief
   C. Pastor
   D. Clan elder

39. Which of these leads prayers in a mosque? (1 mark)
   A. An imam
   B. A tailor
   C. A nurse
   D. A cook

40. Who is the head of a county government? (1 mark)
   A. The MCA
   B. The chief
   C. The Governor
   D. The Speaker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the meaning of democracy. (2 marks)

42. Explain how citizens can support the county government. (4 marks)

43. State three ways in which physical features are important to people. (3 marks)

44. Explain why we say that the compass is useful in a county. (5 marks)

45. Explain why discipline is important in school. (3 marks)

46. Explain the difference between a ceremony and a festival and give one example of each. (4 marks)

47. Write a short motto and explain what it asks pupils to do. (3 marks)

48. State three roles of an MCA. (3 marks)

49. State three reasons why Kenya has county governments. (3 marks)

50. List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place. (4 marks)

51. Explain what a Children's Government is. (2 marks)

52. State two things that a visitor can learn in a museum. (2 marks)

53. State three benefits of democracy in school. (3 marks)

54. Name two duties of a pupil in school. (2 marks)

55. Explain three effects of child abuse on a child. (3 marks)

56. Describe how an ordinary pupil can support the Children's Government. (3 marks)

57. What is a majority? (2 marks)

58. Explain why forgiveness is important for peace. (3 marks)

59. What is a sub-county? (2 marks)

60. A group spent Ksh 900 and earned Ksh 600. Say whether this is a profit or a loss and find the amount. Suggest two reasons why it may have happened. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — South
   North and south are opposite each other on the compass rose.

2. D — 47
   The Constitution of Kenya 2010 created 47 counties.

3. D — The equator
   The equator crosses the middle of Kenya.

4. A — Indian Ocean
   Kenya's coast is on the Indian Ocean.

5. A — Waterfall
   A waterfall is where a river drops over a steep edge.

6. B — March to May
   The long rains are usually from March to May.

7. C — In a strong building
   Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

8. D — The side facing the oncoming traffic
   Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

9. C — October to December
   The short rains usually come between October and December.

10. C — Mombasa
   Fort Jesus is a fort at Mombasa.

11. A — All useful jobs are important
   Every worker contributes to the community.

12. D — It makes buying and selling easier
   Money is a common way of paying for goods and services.

13. D — 7,000
   7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

14. C — The way of life of a community
   Culture is the way of life passed on from generation to generation.

15. B — It gives identity and teaches values
   Culture helps us to know who we are.

16. A — Controlling yourself and following rules
   Discipline is self-control and obeying rules.

17. D — Beating pupils
   Teachers are not allowed to beat pupils.

18. C — To keep everyone safe and help learning
   Rules protect people and help learning.

19. A — A skilled farmer
   People's skills and labour are human resources.

20. B — Helmet
   Helmets protect workers' heads.

21. C — A hotel
   Hotels provide services.

22. D — Stay with the group and not touch machines
   Safety rules protect visitors.

23. B — A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   Industries change raw materials into products or provide services.

24. A — A large building where goods are made with machines
   Factories use machines to make goods.

25. B — A business activity to make goods or provide services
   Enterprises earn money by making goods or services.

26. A — Ksh 300
   700 - 400 = 300.

27. C — Tell a trusted adult
   A trusted adult can help.

28. B — Something you are expected to do
   A duty is a responsibility.

29. B — A garden where pupils can sit and be calm
   A peace garden is calm and beautiful.

30. C — Talk, do not fight
   Talking solves problems peacefully.

31. C — So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   Planning helps activities succeed.

32. C — Making posters and songs on child protection
   Awareness helps protect children.

33. C — Each person has one vote of equal value
   Everyone's vote counts the same.

34. D — Cheating
   Buying votes is unfair.

35. D — Electing a class monitor by voting
   Voting gives everyone a say.

36. B — Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

37. B — A pastor
   Pastors lead worship.

38. B — Chief
   A chief leads a location.

39. A — An imam
   An imam leads prayers.

40. C — The Governor
   The governor leads the county.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Democracy is rule by the people, where everyone has a say in choosing leaders and making decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rule by the people, 1 mark for having a say.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give water, they provide fish and food, and they attract visitors. Accept farming land or electric power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to find our way. It helps mapmakers to draw maps. It helps us to describe where places are. It helps drivers and sailors to travel. It helps us to plan journeys.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 5.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the school orderly, it helps everyone learn, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A ceremony marks a special event in life, such as a wedding. A festival is a big celebration with many people, such as the Lamu Cultural Festival.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It asks pupils to study well and treat others with kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent the ward, make county laws, and approve the budget. Accept checking the governor.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: To bring services closer to people, to let people take part in decisions, and to share development fairly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a group of pupils elected by their classmates to help run the school and speak for pupils, guided by a teacher.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for elected pupils, 1 mark for helping and speaking for pupils.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: How people lived long ago and which tools they used. Accept learning about animals, plants and cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone has a voice, decisions are fair, and pupils obey rules they helped to make.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Follow the school rules and respect others. Accept care for property or do class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pain and illness, fear and sadness, and missing school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Vote for leaders, follow fair instructions, and give ideas through the class representative.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: The larger number of votes, more than any other choice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for larger number, 1 mark for votes.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It ends quarrels, it helps friendships to grow again, and it stops anger from continuing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sub-county is a smaller part of a county. Each county is divided into sub-counties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it is a smaller part, 1 mark for the link with a county.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: It is a loss of Ksh 300. Sales may have been low because the price was too high or not enough people knew about the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for loss, 1 mark for the amount 900 - 600 = 300, 1 mark for each reason.
